To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fragrances are abundant in indoor air, and they are perceived as odors that may cause adverse effects.

(i) indoor levels of the four major abundant airborne fragrances (APN, LIM, LIL, and EUG) may cause odor annoyance and sensory irritation of the eyes and upper respiratory tract, but are unlikely to cause adverse health effects; (ii) the fragrances are not sensitizers of the airways; (iii) effects on breathing rate and heart rate variability by the fragrances are inconsistent; (iv) the fragrances may cause distraction and reduce work performance, but
the abundant fragrances are not expected to cause adverse health effects by inhalation exposure at the typical indoor concentrations.
